questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Census 2011:
1. Sex ratio is expressed as the number of females per 1000 males.
2. India's overall sex ratio was 943.
3. The child sex ratio (0-6 years) in 2011 was higher than in 2001.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Sex ratio is females per 1000 males and the 2011 figure was 943. The child sex ratio actually fell from 927 in 2001 to 919 in 2011, so statement 3 is wrong; this fall is why sex-selective practices stayed a policy concern.
questions.s: Census of India 2011 (Provisional Population Totals); Majid Husain, Population chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about sex ratio in Census 2011:
1. Haryana had the lowest sex ratio among all States and Union Territories.
2. Kerala recorded the highest sex ratio among the States.
3. Puducherry recorded a sex ratio above 1000.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Kerala (1084) was highest among States and Puducherry (1037) also exceeded 1000. Haryana (879) was the lowest among States, but among UTs Daman and Diu (618) was far lower, so 'all States and UTs' makes statement 1 wrong.
questions.s: Census of India 2011; Majid Husain

questions.q: In Census terminology, the 'effective literacy rate' is the number of literates expressed as a percentage of
o: the population aged seven years and above
the population aged fifteen years and above
the population in the age group 5 to 14 years
questions.e: Since 1991 the Census excludes the 0-6 age group when calculating literacy because children that young cannot be judged literate. Using the total population gives the 'crude literacy rate', which is lower.
questions.s: Census of India 2011 (Concepts and Definitions); NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 2

questions.q:
With reference to the criteria for a 'Census Town' in India, consider the following:
1. A minimum population of 5,000.
2. At least 50 per cent of the male main working population engaged in non-agricultural pursuits.
3. A density of population of at least 400 persons per sq km.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A Census Town needs 5,000 population, a density of at least 400 per sq km and at least 75 per cent (not 50 per cent) of male main workers in non-agricultural work. Statutory towns, by contrast, are notified by law (municipality, corporation, cantonment board, notified area committee) regardless of size.
questions.s: Census of India 2011 (Concepts and Definitions); NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about internal migration in India:
1. The Census records migration on the basis of place of birth and place of last residence.
2. Maharashtra is among the largest receiving States of inter-State migrants.
3. Inter-State migration is larger in volume than intra-State migration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Census uses both birth place and last residence. Most movement is short-distance and within the same State (often marriage-related), so intra-State exceeds inter-State migration; Maharashtra and Delhi are the major destination States while Uttar Pradesh and Bihar are the major sending States.
questions.s: Census of India 2011 (Migration Tables); Majid Husain

questions.q:
Statement-I: In India, rural-to-rural movement forms the largest stream of internal migration.
Statement-II: Marriage is the dominant reason for migration among women.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Most women move to the husband's village after marriage, and women form the bulk of migrants, so the rural-to-rural stream is the biggest. Male migration is more job-driven and tilts towards urban destinations.
questions.s: Census of India 2011 (Migration Tables); NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 2

questions.q: Which one of the following States had the highest density of population among the States of India in Census 2011?
questions.e: Bihar (about 1,100 persons per sq km) is the densest State because of its fertile Gangetic alluvium, flat terrain and flood-renewed soils, with West Bengal second. Kerala is also dense but ranks below both.
questions.s: Census of India 2011; NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 1

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about population density in India:
1. India's density in Census 2011 was 325 persons per sq km.
2. Among the States, Arunachal Pradesh had the lowest density.
3. Among Union Territories, Delhi had the highest density.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Density rose from 325 in 2001 to 382 in 2011, so statement 1 gives the older figure. Arunachal Pradesh (about 17) is the sparsest State because of rugged terrain, and Delhi (over 11,000) is the densest UT.
questions.s: Census of India 2011; NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 1

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about urbanisation in Census 2011 are correct?
1. About 31 per cent of India's population lived in urban areas.
2. For the first time since Independence, the absolute increase in population was larger in urban areas than in rural areas.
3. Kerala was the most urbanised State.
4. The number of million-plus cities and urban agglomerations was 53.
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: urban share was 31.16 per cent, the urban increment overtook the rural one for the first time, and there were 53 million-plus cities. Goa (about 62 per cent), not Kerala, was the most urbanised State.
questions.s: Census of India 2011 (Provisional Population Totals); Majid Husain

questions.q: Which one of the following was the most populous urban agglomeration in India in Census 2011?
questions.e: Greater Mumbai (about 18.4 million) was the largest urban agglomeration, ahead of Delhi (about 16.3 million) and Kolkata (about 14.1 million). An urban agglomeration is a continuous urban spread including a town and its adjoining outgrowths.
questions.s: Census of India 2011 (Cities and UAs); NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 1

questions.q:
Match List-I (Census 2011 feature) with List-II (State/UT) and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I
A. Lowest density among States
B. Highest sex ratio among States
C. Highest density among Union Territories
D. Highest density among States
List-II
1. Delhi
2. Bihar
3. Arunachal Pradesh
4. Kerala
questions.e: Arunachal Pradesh is the sparsest State because of its mountainous, forested terrain; Kerala has a sex ratio of 1084; Delhi is the densest UT and Bihar the densest State. Delhi's density comes from a small area with a very large urban population.
questions.s: Census of India 2011; Majid Husain, Population chapter

questions.q: Which one of the following census years is called the 'Year of the Great Divide' in India's demographic history, and why?
o: 1951, because the first census of independent India was held then
1901, because the twentieth century began with a sharp rise in birth rate
1971, because the death rate fell below the birth rate for the first time
1921, because population which had declined in the previous decade has grown continuously since then
questions.e: The 1911-21 decade saw a decline due to the 1918 influenza epidemic and famines; from 1921 onwards India has seen sustained growth as mortality fell through better health care and famine control. The Great Divide is thus a turning point in the growth trend, not the date of any one census.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Population chapter; NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 1

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Census is a subject in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule.
2. Census in India is conducted under the Census Act, 1948.
3. Census 2011 was the fifteenth census of India since 1872.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Census (entry 69 of the Union List) is conducted by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Census Act 1948. Counting from the first (non-synchronous) census of 1872, 2011 was the fifteenth and the seventh since Independence.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Seventh Schedule; Census of India 2011

questions.q:
Statement-I: As per NFHS-5 (2019-21), India's Total Fertility Rate fell below the replacement level.
Statement-II: Replacement-level fertility is the average number of children per woman needed for a population to replace itself from one generation to the next, ignoring migration.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: NFHS-5 reported a TFR of 2.0, below the replacement level of about 2.1. Statement-II is a correct definition, but it does not explain why India's fertility fell; falling fertility reflects education, contraceptive use and later marriage.
questions.s: NFHS-5 National Report (MoHFW, IIPS), 2021

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The dependency ratio relates the population aged below 15 and above 64 to the working-age population.
2. A demographic dividend automatically leads to faster economic growth irrespective of employment and skill levels.
3. A demographic dividend arises when the share of the working-age population is large relative to dependents.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A falling dependency ratio opens a window of opportunity, but the gain materialises only if the extra workers get education, skills and jobs. Without them the dividend can turn into unemployment, so statement 2 is wrong.
questions.s: Economic Survey 2018-19 (Ch on Demographics); NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 2

questions.q: The long-term objective of the National Population Policy, 2000 was to achieve a stable population by which one of the following years?
questions.e: NPP 2000 set an immediate objective of meeting unmet contraception needs, a medium-term goal of bringing the TFR to replacement level by 2010, and the long-term goal of a stable population by 2045, consistent with sustainable development.
questions.s: National Population Policy 2000 (MoHFW); Majid Husain

questions.q:
How many of the following pairs of data source and agency are correctly matched?
1. Sample Registration System : Office of the Registrar General of India
2. National Family Health Survey : International Institute for Population Sciences
3. Periodic Labour Force Survey : Labour Bureau
4. Annual Survey of Industries : Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
questions.e: SRS (birth, death and infant-mortality estimates) is run by the Registrar General and NFHS by IIPS Mumbai as the nodal agency for MoHFW. PLFS and the Annual Survey of Industries are conducted by the National Statistics Office of MoSPI, not by the Labour Bureau or DPIIT.
questions.s: ORGI website; MoHFW; MoSPI

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about literacy in Census 2011:
1. Kerala had the highest literacy rate among the States.
2. The gap between male and female literacy rates narrowed compared to 2001.
3. Rajasthan had the lowest literacy rate among the States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Kerala (93.91 per cent) was highest, and the male-female gap narrowed from about 21.6 points in 2001 to about 16.7 points in 2011 because female literacy rose faster. Bihar (63.82 per cent), not Rajasthan, was lowest among the States.
questions.s: Census of India 2011 (Literacy); NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 2

questions.q:
Statement-I: The child sex ratio (0-6 years) is considered a more sensitive indicator of gender discrimination than the overall sex ratio.
Statement-II: The overall sex ratio is influenced by migration and adult mortality differences, whereas the 0-6 ratio mainly reflects practices at or soon after birth.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Adult sex ratios shift with male out-migration and unequal life expectancy, which mask discrimination. The 0-6 ratio captures sex-selective abortion and neglect of girl children, which is why the PCPNDT Act 1994 and Beti Bachao Beti Padhao target it.
questions.s: Census of India 2011; PIB on Beti Bachao Beti Padhao

questions.q: Which one of the following States recorded a negative decadal population growth rate between Census 2001 and Census 2011?
questions.e: Nagaland was the only State with a negative growth rate (about minus 0.6 per cent) in 2001-11, partly attributed to data issues and out-migration after a very high growth in 1991-2001. Kerala had the lowest positive growth rate.
questions.s: Census of India 2011 (Provisional Population Totals)

questions.q:
Arrange the following States in the descending order of their population as per Census 2011:
1. Bihar
2. Maharashtra
3. Uttar Pradesh
4. West Bengal
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Uttar Pradesh (about 20 crore) is first, then Maharashtra (about 11.2 crore), Bihar (about 10.4 crore) and West Bengal (about 9.1 crore). Bihar is the third most populous State despite having a much smaller area than Maharashtra.
questions.s: Census of India 2011

questions.q: A settlement has a population of 7,000, a density of 450 persons per sq km and 80 per cent of its male main workers in non-agricultural activities, but it is governed by a gram panchayat. How would the Census classify this settlement?
questions.e: It meets all three demographic criteria for a Census Town (5,000 population, 400 density, 75 per cent non-agricultural male workers). It is not a Statutory Town because no municipality, corporation or notified town area committee has been established by law.
questions.s: Census of India 2011 (Concepts and Definitions)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) in Census 2011:
1. Nagaland had the highest proportion of Scheduled Tribes among the States.
2. Punjab had the highest proportion of Scheduled Castes among the States.
3. Madhya Pradesh had the largest Scheduled Tribe population in absolute numbers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Punjab (about 32 per cent) has the largest SC share and Madhya Pradesh the largest ST numbers. Mizoram (about 94 per cent) has the highest ST share among States, ahead of Nagaland (about 86 per cent), so statement 1 is wrong.
questions.s: Census of India 2011 (SC/ST data); Majid Husain

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about NFHS-5 (2019-21):
1. It reported a sex ratio of the total population above 1000 females per 1000 males.
2. India's Total Fertility Rate was reported as 2.0.
3. The International Institute for Population Sciences is the nodal agency for NFHS.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NFHS-5 found 1020 females per 1000 males for the first time in NFHS history, and a TFR of 2.0. These are sample-survey estimates, so they differ from Census counts (943 in 2011).
questions.s: NFHS-5 National Report (MoHFW, IIPS), 2021

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a 'push' factor behind rural-to-urban migration in India?
o: Better educational and medical facilities in cities
questions.e: Push factors are conditions that drive people out of the origin area: poverty, unemployment, landlessness and natural hazards. Better services and jobs in cities are pull factors that attract migrants.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the location of industries:
1. Industries using heavy weight-losing raw materials tend to be located near the raw material source.
2. Footloose industries such as software are strongly tied to the source of raw materials.
3. Sugar and cement are examples of such industries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: If most of the raw material's weight is lost in processing (cane, limestone, iron ore), it is cheaper to process near the source rather than carry waste. Footloose industries use light, low-weight inputs and depend on skilled labour, so they are not tied to raw material sources.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 6; Majid Husain

questions.q: Which one of the following integrated steel plants is NOT a unit of the Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL)?
questions.e: Visakhapatnam Steel Plant belongs to Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL), a separate public sector company; it is a coastal plant using imported coking coal. SAIL (formed 1973) runs Bhilai, Bokaro, Rourkela, Durgapur and Burnpur.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Industries chapter; Ministry of Steel

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about public sector steel plants set up after Independence:
1. The Rourkela plant was set up with German collaboration.
2. The Durgapur plant was set up with British collaboration.
3. The Bokaro plant was set up with American collaboration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: During the Second Plan, Rourkela (Odisha) was set up with German help, Durgapur (West Bengal) with British help and Bhilai (Chhattisgarh) with Soviet help. Bokaro (Jharkhand) was also built with Soviet assistance, not American.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Industries chapter; NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 6

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Chotanagpur plateau region is India's leading region of heavy industries, especially iron and steel.
Statement-II: It has coal, iron ore, manganese and other minerals concentrated in a compact area, with access to the Hugli port and the Kolkata market.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Coal of the Damodar valley and iron ore of Singhbhum and the Odisha border lie close together, so steel plants such as Jamshedpur, Bokaro and Burnpur grew up here. Cheap raw materials plus the Hugli outlet explain the region's concentration of heavy industry.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 6; Majid Husain

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the cotton textile industry in India:
1. The industry is entirely concentrated within the cotton-growing black soil regions.
2. The first successful cotton mill was established at Mumbai in 1854.
3. Coimbatore developed as a major centre with the help of cheap hydroelectricity from the Pykara project.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Mumbai's early lead came from its port, humid climate that reduces yarn breakage, capital and nearby black-soil cotton. Because cotton is a pure raw material that is light to transport, the industry has spread to Coimbatore, Kanpur and elsewhere, so it is not confined to the cotton belt.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 6; Majid Husain

questions.q:
Statement-I: Most of India's jute mills are located along the banks of the Hugli river in West Bengal.
Statement-II: The Hugli region offers cheap water transport, abundant water for processing the fibre and proximity to the jute-growing delta and the Kolkata port.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Jute is bulky, needs soft water for retting and is exported through Kolkata, so mills clustered on the Hugli. After Partition, the main jute-growing districts went to East Pakistan while the mills stayed in India, which pushed India to expand domestic jute cultivation.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 6; Majid Husain

questions.q: Which one of the following is the most appropriate reason for the shift of the sugar industry from northern India to the peninsular States, particularly Maharashtra?
o: Sugar is a weight-gaining industry that needs to be near the market
Peninsular India gets frequent winter rainfall that improves cane yield
North Indian rivers are no longer suitable for irrigation
Cane grown in the tropical peninsular region has a higher sucrose content and a longer crushing season
questions.e: Tropical cane gives higher sucrose recovery and the crushing season is longer than in the subtropical north. The cooperative sector in Maharashtra also helped, while sugar is a weight-losing industry located near cane fields.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 6; Majid Husain

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the cement industry:
1. Limestone is the principal raw material.
2. Bauxite is the chief raw material used in cement manufacture.
3. Gypsum is added to the clinker to control the setting time.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Cement is made from limestone with clay or shale, burnt in kilns using coal, and gypsum is ground with the clinker to slow setting. Bauxite is the ore of aluminium, not a cement material.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 6; Majid Husain

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the aluminium industry in India:
1. Smelting of aluminium requires very large quantities of electricity.
2. The smelter at Renukoot in Uttar Pradesh draws power from the Rihand project.
3. The alumina refinery of NALCO is located at Korba.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Power is a major share of smelting cost, so smelters are sited near power sources such as Rihand (Renukoot) and Hirakud. NALCO's refinery is at Damanjodi in Odisha and its smelter at Angul; Korba in Chhattisgarh has the BALCO smelter.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Industries chapter

questions.q: Which one of the following was India's first large fertilizer factory, started in 1951?
questions.e: Sindri (then in Bihar, now Jharkhand) was set up in 1951 to make ammonium sulphate from coal-based raw materials. Nangal (Punjab) was a hydel-power-based plant set up later, and plants like Trombay and Namrup came after.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Industries chapter; NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 6

questions.q:
How many of the following refinery-State pairs are correctly matched?
1. Digboi : Assam
2. Mathura : Haryana
3. Koyali : Gujarat
4. Barauni : Bihar
questions.e: Digboi (India's oldest refinery), Koyali near Vadodara and Barauni are in the stated States. Mathura refinery is in Uttar Pradesh and was built to supply the northern markets.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Industries chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Special Economic Zones (SEZ):
1. SEZ units are treated as part of the Domestic Tariff Area for customs duty.
2. The SEZ Act was passed in 2005.
3. Kandla was Asia's first export processing zone, set up in 1965.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The SEZ policy came in April 2000, replaced by the SEZ Act 2005 (in force from 2006); Kandla in Gujarat started as an EPZ in 1965. SEZs are deemed foreign territory for trade operations, duties and tariffs, which is the incentive for exporters.
questions.s: Ministry of Commerce and Industry (SEZ); Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the dedicated freight corridors and industrial corridors:
1. The Amritsar-Kolkata Industrial Corridor is aligned to the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor.
2. The Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor is aligned to the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor.
3. The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor runs from JNPT (Mumbai) to Dadri.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Industrial corridors are built around freight corridors so that factories near the line get cheap bulk transport. DMIC follows the Western DFC (JNPT-Dadri), while AKIC follows the Eastern DFC (Ludhiana-Dankuni).
questions.s: Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT, NICDC); PIB

questions.q:
Which of the following are among the 'Eight Core Industries' of India?
1. Coal
2. Fertilizers
3. Cotton textiles
4. Cement
5. Natural gas
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The eight core industries are coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilizers, steel, cement and electricity. Cotton textiles is a consumer-goods industry and is not in the index.
questions.s: Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q:
Arrange the following industrial policy measures in chronological order:
1. Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956
2. Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951
3. New Industrial Policy, 1991
4. Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: IPR 1948 started the mixed economy, the IDRA 1951 gave it the licensing framework, IPR 1956 classified industries into Schedules A, B and C, and the 1991 policy dismantled licensing.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Industrial Policy)

questions.q:
Statement-I: Cotton textile mills developed early in Mumbai.
Statement-II: Mumbai is itself the largest cotton-growing area of India.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Mumbai's advantages were its port, humid climate, capital from merchants and access to cotton from the Deccan black-soil hinterland. The cotton is grown in the hinterland, not in the island city itself.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 6; Majid Husain

questions.q: Which one of the following industries is LEAST likely to be a footloose industry?
questions.e: Footloose industries use light, low-weight inputs and are not tied to any raw material source. Sugar uses bulky, perishable cane that loses sucrose quickly after harvest, so mills must stand in the cane fields.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 6

questions.q:
Match List-I (Rail production unit) with List-II (Location) and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I
A. Integral Coach Factory
B. Diesel Locomotive Works
C. Rail Coach Factory
D. Diesel-Loco Modernisation Works
List-II
1. Kapurthala
2. Patiala
3. Perambur
4. Varanasi
questions.e: ICF is at Perambur (Chennai), DLW at Varanasi, the Rail Coach Factory at Kapurthala (Punjab) and DMW at Patiala. These transport-equipment plants are public sector units under the Railway Ministry.
questions.s: Ministry of Railways; Majid Husain

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about silk production in India:
1. India is the only country that produces all four commercial varieties of silk: mulberry, tasar, eri and muga.
2. Muga silk is produced almost exclusively in Assam.
3. Eri silk is produced exclusively in Kerala.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Mulberry is the main variety (Karnataka leads), tasar is common in Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh, and muga is the golden silk unique to Assam. Eri is a North-eastern speciality (Assam and neighbours), not a Kerala product.
questions.s: Central Silk Board; Ministry of Textiles

questions.q: Which one of the following shipbuilding yards is located on the east coast of India?
questions.e: Hindustan Shipyard is in Visakhapatnam on the Bay of Bengal. Mazagon Dock, Cochin Shipyard and Goa Shipyard are all on the west coast.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Industries chapter

questions.q:
Match List-I (Craft/Product) with List-II (Town) and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I
A. Glass bangles
B. Brassware
C. Locks
D. Carpets
List-II
1. Aligarh
2. Bhadohi
3. Moradabad
4. Firozabad
questions.e: Firozabad is the glass centre, Moradabad the brassware centre, Aligarh the lock centre and Bhadohi-Mirzapur the carpet belt. Many of these small clusters in Uttar Pradesh grew around local craft traditions and skilled labour.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Industries chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the paper industry in India:
1. The industry uses a weight-gaining raw material and is therefore market-oriented.
2. Bamboo, bagasse and recycled paper are important raw materials.
3. Nepanagar in Madhya Pradesh has India's first newsprint mill.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Paper uses bulky fibre raw materials that lose weight in processing, so mills tend to stand near forests or cane areas rather than markets. Nepanagar's newsprint mill started in the 1950s.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Industries chapter

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the principal factors in Weber's theory of industrial location?
questions.e: Weber's least-cost theory takes transport cost as the main factor, modified by labour cost and agglomeration (or deglomeration) forces. Government subsidies and policy are not part of the original model, though they matter in modern location decisions.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Industries chapter; NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 6

questions.q:
How many of the following handloom products are correctly matched with their State?
1. Pochampally : Telangana
2. Chanderi : Madhya Pradesh
3. Paithani : Maharashtra
4. Sambalpuri : Odisha
questions.e: All four are correct: Pochampally ikat (Telangana), Chanderi (Madhya Pradesh), Paithani (Paithan, Maharashtra) and Sambalpuri ikat (Odisha). Such clusters typically rest on traditional weaver communities.
questions.s: Ministry of Textiles; Nitin Singhania, Indian Art and Culture

questions.q: A company wants to set up a new sugar mill. Which one of the following would be the most suitable location, and why?
o: Near a major port, because sugar is mainly exported
Near a large city, because sugar is a weight-gaining product
Near coalfields, because coal is the main input
Close to sugarcane fields, because cane is bulky and loses sucrose if transport is delayed
questions.e: Cane is a weight-losing, perishable raw material, so the sugar content drops quickly after harvesting; mills are therefore built within a short haul of the fields. Market proximity matters little because refined sugar is light and durable.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 6
